steps.title: Documents (web) — upload, category, audience, schedule, delete; announcements attach a document
steps.goal: Every active member sees a Documents entry in the org navigation and, at `/o/<slug>/documents`, the documents published to an audience they belong to, filterable by category, with Open (PDF, images) or Download (Word, Excel, text) buttons on one-hour signed URLs. A `documents.upload` holder uploads files up to 50 MB from the eight-type allow-list with title, category, audience group and publish time (now or scheduled), edits that metadata, resumes or discards incomplete uploads, and deletes documents (objects removed by the cron drain). Announcement managers attach a published document to an announcement through a real picker (replacing 3.5a's disabled placeholder) with an audience-mismatch warning, and announcement lists show a paper-clip link. `@church/db` gains `queries/documents.ts` (deferred by 1.7a). Documents never push — `notification_kind` has no `document` value — and the UI says so.

## Goal
When you finish, every active member of a church sees a **Documents** entry in the org navigation and, at `/o/<slug>/documents`, the documents published to an audience they belong to, filterable by category, with an Open button (PDF and images open in a new tab) or a Download button (Word, Excel and text files, which browsers cannot render) backed by one-hour signed URLs. A leader holding `documents.upload` can upload a file of up to 50 MB from the allow-list (PDF, JPG, PNG, TXT, Word, Excel) with a title, an optional category, an audience group and a publish time (now or scheduled), edit that metadata later, resume or discard an incomplete upload, and delete a document (the object is removed by the cron drain). Announcement managers can attach a published document to an announcement: 3.5a's disabled "Attach a document" placeholder becomes a real picker and the announcement lists show a paper-clip link that opens the document. Documents never send a push on their own — `notification_kind` has no `document` value — so the form says so and points at "create an announcement and attach this document". The mobile app is untouched (5.4b).

## Build

Export from `packages/domain/src/index.ts`.
3. **Form schema** `apps/web/src/features/documents/form-schema.ts`: `documentUploadFormSchema` = `{ title 1–160, description optional ≤ 4000 (only if the column exists), category optional (documentCategorySchema), audience_group_id uuid (required in the UI — store the `everyone` system group for "All attendees", never null, as 3.5a does), publish_mode: 'now' | 'schedule', publish_at_local (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm`, required when 'schedule'), file_name, mime_type ∈ BUCKETS.documents.allowedMimeTypes, file_size_bytes ≤ effective cap }` with the message "Documents can be PDF, JPG, PNG, TXT, Word or Excel files up to 50 MB"; `documentEditFormSchema` = the metadata subset plus `publish_mode`/`publish_at_local`; `toDocumentInput(form, tz, now)` producing what `documentSchema` accepts; `resolveDocumentMime(fileName: string, reportedType: string): { ext, mime } | null` — pure, string arguments so the Server Action re-runs it (mirror `resolveBulletinMime`): trust `reportedType` when non-empty and `isAllowedMime('documents', reportedType)`, else map the lowercase extension (`pdf`, `jpg`/`jpeg`, `png`, `txt`, `doc`, `docx`, `xls`, `xlsx`) to its canonical MIME, else `null`; `ext = extensionForMime(mime)`. ## Constraints
- Do not touch `supabase/` (no migrations; `9999_init.sql` may be frozen — check the HANDOFF ledger; if a schema fact blocks you, stop and ask rather than editing SQL), `apps/web/vercel.json`, `proxy.ts`, `next.config.ts`, CSP, `/admin`, sermons, share links, users, bulletins (beyond reading them as the pattern), `src/lib/push/*`, or `apps/mobile` (5.4b). Do not build custom group management (5.5), join codes (5.6), or any public share page for documents (not planned).
- Never hold an elevated key in the browser; every write goes through Server Actions with the user client under RLS; `mintDocumentUrl` uses the user client so `storage.objects` RLS decides.
- Reuse, do not duplicate: one uploader (`src/features/uploads/*`), one date module (`src/lib/dates.ts`), one MIME table (`BUCKETS` + `extensionForMime` / `isAllowedMime`), one audience select. Additive changes to `@church/domain` / `@church/db` only, each with a test and a HANDOFF note.

steps.prompt:
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is step 5.4b "Documents (mobile) — list by category, open or share files, linked document on announcements, More tab row" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/PLAN.md` §6, §9 and §11 item (4), and `docs/DESIGN.md` §6 (the `documents` row and the "Storage policies" paragraph), §7 (bucket table; "Android PDF (bulletins)"), §10 and §11 Phase 2 before writing code. Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
When you finish, a member opens **Documents** from the More tab of the Anacast app and sees the documents published to an audience they belong to, grouped by category with a chip filter, each row showing kind, title, size and date. Tapping a row opens a detail screen whose "Open document" button downloads the file over a one-hour signed URL and hands it to an installed viewer — PDF, Word, Excel and text through an Android `ACTION_VIEW` intent with the exact MIME type, images inline — and falls back to the system Share sheet when no app can open the type. An announcement that carries a linked document shows a document card in `announcements/[id]` (replacing 4.2a's `TODO(5.4)` comment), and a document the member may not see (audience mismatch, unpublished, deleted) is simply absent — never an error that hints it exists. Nothing changes in the database, the web app or the push pipeline: documents have no notification kind.

## Inputs / prior state
- 4.1a–4.3 produced the app shell: `supabase` client, `AppQueryProvider` (kv-store persister; `shouldPersistQuery` excludes every `queryKeys.signedUrl(…)` key), `useSession()`, `useActiveOrg()` → `{ org: { org_id, slug, name, status }, permissions, personId, householdId, orgs, switchOrg }`, `Screen` / `LoadingState` / `ErrorState` / `EmptyState`, `publicEnv()`, `src/theme.ts` + `src/theme/tokens.ts`, `LinkifiedText`, `src/lib/signed-url.ts` (`useSignedUrl(bucket, path, opts)` → `{ url, expiresAt, isExpired, remint }`, non-hook `getSignedUrl(bucket, path)`, `isSignedUrlExpired`), `src/features/bulletins/{BulletinList,BulletinDetail,OpenPdf.ts}` with `openBulletinFile({ bucket, path, mimeType, fileName })` (legacy `expo-file-system/legacy` download to `cacheDirectory` → `getContentUriAsync` → `IntentLauncher.startActivityAsync('android.intent.action.VIEW', { data, flags: 1, type })`, browser fallback on `ActivityNotFoundException`, iOS branch marked "Phase 3 (6.4) verifies"), `pickOpener(mimeType, platform)` → `'intent' | 'inline_image' | 'share' | 'browser'`, the 4.2a "Showing saved content — you appear to be offline" bar, `src/features/feed/{AnnouncementCard,AnnouncementDetail}.tsx` (the detail carries the `TODO(5.4)` comment where a linked document should render), `src/features/more/MoreMenu.tsx` (rows Bulletins, Notification settings, Change password, Switch church, Sign out, footer links), `src/lib/deep-links.ts` (`resolveNotificationTarget` — unchanged here: no document push exists). If 5.2a/5.3b ran before you, `MoreMenu` may already carry Directory and Calendar rows.
- Mobile dependencies already installed by 4.1a/4.2a via `npx expo install`: `expo-file-system`, `expo-intent-launcher`, `expo-sharing`, `expo-web-browser`, `expo-image`, `react-native-paper`, `@tanstack/react-query`, `expo-router`. Nothing new is needed for this step.
- Web 5.4a shipped in `@church/db`: `queries/documents.ts` — `listPublishedDocuments(db, orgId, { category?, limit? })` (= `publish_at <= now()`; RLS additionally applies `user_in_group`), `listDocuments`, `getDocument(db, id)`, `listDocumentCategories(db, orgId)`; `keys.ts` — `queryKeys.documents.list(orgId)`, `.documents.detail(id)`, `.documents.categories(orgId)`, `.signedUrl(bucket, path)`. In `@church/domain`: `BUCKETS.documents` (50 MiB; eight MIME types: `application/pdf`, `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `text/plain`, `application/msword`, `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document`, `application/vnd.ms-excel`, `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`), `documents.ts` — `documentKind(mime)` → `'pdf' | 'image' | 'text' | 'word' | 'excel'` and `DOCUMENT_KIND_LABELS`; `limits.ts` — `SIGNED_URL_TTL_SECONDS`, `SIGNED_URL_CACHE_MS`; `dates.ts` formatting helpers; `errors.ts` — `toDomainError`. Read the real signatures first (5.4a's HANDOFF hand-off line names them); if 5.4a's agent named something differently, follow the code and note the difference in HANDOFF.
- Database facts (DESIGN §6; `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql`): `documents` select for members = active member ∧ `publish_at <= now()` ∧ `app.user_in_group(audience_group_id)` (null = everyone); `storage.objects` select on bucket `documents` = `app.can_read_object` = the row is visible to the caller — the app signs URLs with the member's session and never proxies bytes; `announcements.document_id` is a nullable FK, so an announcement stays visible when its document is not; the row shape is `id, org_id, title, category, audience_group_id, storage_path, mime_type, file_size_bytes, publish_at, created_by` (+ `description` if 5.4a found the column — read `packages/db/src/database.types.ts`). `notification_kind` has no `document` value: no push payload will ever carry `/documents/<id>`, so `resolveNotificationTarget` and 4.3's preference switches stay as they are.
- Founder decision 10 (Supabase Free): files are ≤ 50 MiB and every download counts toward the 5 GB monthly egress — cache files by document id and never re-download an unchanged document.

## Build
1. **Data hooks** `src/features/documents/useDocuments.ts`: `useDocuments(orgId)` = `useQuery({ queryKey: queryKeys.documents.list(orgId), queryFn: () => listPublishedDocuments(supabase, orgId, {}), staleTime: 5 * 60_000 })` — filter by category in memory (one query, persisted for offline reading); `useDocument(id)` = `useQuery({ queryKey: queryKeys.documents.detail(id), queryFn: () => getDocument(supabase, id) })` with `initialData` taken from the list cache when the row is present; pure helpers in `src/features/documents/format.ts`: `groupByCategory(rows)` → `{ category: string | null; items }[]` sorted by category name, `null` ("Other") last, items `publish_at desc`; `categoriesOf(rows)` → sorted distinct categories; `documentSizeLabel(bytes)` (KB under 1 MB, otherwise MB with one decimal); `documentFileName(row)` → `<title slug>.<ext from mime via extensionForMime>` (safe for the file system, never the storage uuid). Pull-to-refresh invalidates `queryKeys.documents.list(orgId)`.
2. **List** `app/(app)/documents/index.tsx` + `src/features/documents/DocumentList.tsx`: header "Documents"; a horizontal chip row built from `categoriesOf(rows)` with "All" first (no second query — comment why); `SectionList` from `groupByCategory` (a section header per category; a flat list when no row has a category); row = kind icon by `documentKind`, title, `category · size · <published date>` through the domain date helpers; tap → `documents/[id]`; `RefreshControl`; empty state "Your church has not shared any documents yet"; error state with Retry; when the persisted cache serves rows and the refetch fails, keep them with the 4.2a offline bar (reuse the component; do not copy it).
3. **Detail and open** `app/(app)/documents/[id].tsx` + `src/features/documents/DocumentDetail.tsx`: title, description (when present in the row type), category, `DOCUMENT_KIND_LABELS[kind]`, size, published date; primary button "Open document"; secondary "Share". Open logic: do NOT copy `openBulletinFile` — generalise it: move the download → content-URI → intent → fallback body from `src/features/bulletins/OpenPdf.ts` into `src/lib/open-file.ts` as `openStoredFile({ bucket, path, mimeType, fileName, cacheKey, expectedSize })`, keep `openBulletinFile` as a thin wrapper so 4.2a's callers and tests stay untouched, and call `openStoredFile({ bucket: 'documents', path: row.storage_path, mimeType: row.mime_type, fileName: documentFileName(row), cacheKey: row.id, expectedSize: row.file_size_bytes })` here. Extend `pickOpener(mimeType, platform)` (table-tested): Android → `application/pdf`, the two Word types, the two Excel types and `text/plain` → `'intent'` (ACTION_VIEW with the exact MIME type; Google Docs/Sheets, WPS, Drive PDF viewer or the system viewer pick it up), `image/jpeg` / `image/png` → `'inline_image'`; iOS (untested until 6.4) → `'share'` for everything but images. Fallback chain inside `openStoredFile`: when no activity handles the intent (`ActivityNotFoundException` or `startActivityAsync` rejecting) → `expo-sharing` `shareAsync(localUri, { mimeType })` with the toast "No app can open this file. Choose an app to share it with."; only when `Sharing.isAvailableAsync()` is false → `WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync(signedUrl)`. Cache: `FileSystem.cacheDirectory + 'anacast-files/' + cacheKey + '.' + ext`; before downloading, `getInfoAsync` — reuse the cached file when it exists and its `size` equals `expectedSize`, otherwise delete and re-download; on a 403 or an expired signed URL → `remint()` once and retry, then the friendly error "This file could not be opened. Pull to refresh and try again."; show a progress indicator (`createDownloadResumable` progress callback) during download.
4. **Images**: `image/jpeg` / `image/png` render inline on the detail screen with `expo-image` (`contentFit: 'contain'`), same "Share" button — the 4.2a bulletin pattern.
5. **Linked document on announcements**: in `src/features/feed/AnnouncementDetail.tsx` replace the `TODO(5.4)` comment with `LinkedDocumentCard` (`src/features/documents/LinkedDocumentCard.tsx`): when `announcement.document_id` is set, `useDocument(document_id)`; while loading render a small skeleton; when the query returns a row render a card (kind icon, title, size, chevron) that navigates to `documents/[id]`; when it returns no row (RLS-hidden, scheduled, deleted) render nothing — no "not available" text, because the member must not learn that a restricted document exists. In `src/features/feed/AnnouncementCard.tsx` show a paper-clip icon when `document_id` is set (presence of the id only — no query per card). If `getAnnouncement` / `listFeed` do not select `document_id`, add the column to their explicit column lists additively (with a test) and record it.
6. **More tab**: in `src/features/more/MoreMenu.tsx` add the row Documents → `/documents` in the DESIGN §10 order ("Phase 2/3 add Directory, Calendar, Documents, Surveys, My household …"): after Directory and Calendar when 5.2a/5.3b already added them, otherwise directly under Bulletins. Keep the remaining rows and the footer untouched.
7. **Routing**: register `documents/index` and `documents/[id]` in the stack layout where 4.x declares `bulletins/[id]` (titles "Documents" / "Document"); `documents/[id]` must work when opened cold with only an id (same rule as `announcements/[id]`), because the announcement card may be the first screen a member reaches after a push tap.
8. **Accessibility and copy**: rows are `Pressable` with `accessibilityRole="button"` and `accessibilityLabel` "<title>, <kind label>, <size>"; text sizes respect the system font scale; all strings English, sentence case; the empty state, the no-viewer toast and the open-failure message are the only new copy.
9. **Tests** (Vitest, node; `vi.mock` for `@church/db` and every `expo-*` module; use whichever renderer 4.x already uses — add no test library): `format.test.ts` (`groupByCategory` puts `null` last and sorts items newest first; `categoriesOf` dedupes; `documentSizeLabel` 512 KB / 1.5 MB; `documentFileName` slug + extension for a docx row), the extended `pickOpener` table (every MIME in `BUCKETS.documents.allowedMimeTypes` yields a defined opener on `android` and on `ios`), `open-file.test.ts` (intent rejection → `Sharing.shareAsync` called once; sharing unavailable → `openBrowserAsync`; cached file with matching size → no download; size mismatch → re-download; 403 → `remint` called once then success), `LinkedDocumentCard.test.tsx` (renders nothing when the query resolves to `null`; renders the title when a row exists), `openBulletinFile` still passes its 4.2a tests unchanged.
10. **Docs**: `docs/MEDIA.md` (4.4) — a "Documents" section: which app opens each type on Android, the share fallback, the cache path and size check, the egress note; `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` device checklist — a "Documents (5.4b)" block holding the manual checks from Verify; `apps/mobile/README.md` "Mobile playback and files" — one line for documents.

## Constraints
- Mobile native dependency versions come only from `npx expo install <pkg>`; this step needs no new native module — if you believe one is required, stop and ask. `react` stays `catalog:` (19.2.3).
- No elevated key on the device; the app reads `documents` and signs URLs with the member's session under RLS. Never persist signed URLs (`queryKeys.signedUrl` + `meta.persist: false`).
- Do not touch `supabase/`, `apps/web`, `src/lib/deep-links.ts`, push registration, or `settings/notifications`. Additive changes to `@church/db` / `@church/domain` only if 5.4a missed something you need, each with a test and a HANDOFF note.
- Do not build directory, events, join-code or survey screens; do not add a documents push preference (there is no such kind); do not add a documents web view.
- No model identifiers in commits or files; no secrets; never `supabase db push` or `supabase db reset`.

steps.goal: Leaders holding `announcements.create` or `org.settings` get a Groups page at `/o/<slug>/groups` that lists the six system audience groups read-only (each explained from the church's youth/adult settings, no counts) and lets them create, rename, describe and delete custom groups — deletion shows what happens to the announcements, documents and calendars that target the group and is blocked by surveys — and manage each custom group's members at `/o/<slug>/groups/<groupId>` with a searchable picker fed by `directory_persons` (whole-household add, badges for inactive/deceased/no-account members). Every audience select (announcements, documents, calendars; surveys later) lists custom groups under a separator with a Manage groups link. No migration, no mobile UI; `docs/RLS.md` and `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` gain the custom-groups paragraphs.

## Goal
When you finish, a leader holding `announcements.create` **or** `org.settings` (PLAN §4: "custom groups = `announcements.create` or `org.settings`") sees a **Groups** entry in the org navigation and, at `/o/<slug>/groups`, the six system audience groups (All attendees, Members, Non-member attendees, Youth, Men, Women — read-only, each with a plain-English explanation of who is in it computed from the church's settings) followed by the church's custom groups. They can create a custom group (name, optional description), rename it, edit its description, delete it after a confirmation that spells out what happens to the announcements, documents and calendars that target it, and manage its members on `/o/<slug>/groups/<groupId>` with a searchable picker fed by the directory views. Every existing audience select (announcements 3.5a, documents 5.4a, calendars 5.3a — and surveys in 6.1) lists the custom groups under a separator with a "Manage groups" link, so a custom group can be the audience of an announcement the moment it exists. Members without the permission pair see nothing new: `/groups` is 403 for them, and the mobile app is untouched (custom groups only change which announcements, documents and calendar entries a member sees and which pushes reach them; there is no member-facing UI).

## Inputs / prior state
- Schema (1.2/1.3, `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql`, sections (3), (5), (7), (8)) — read it, do not change it: `audience_groups` (`id, org_id, kind audience_kind not null, name text not null, description, created_by, created_at, updated_at`; `unique (org_id, name)`; partial unique `(org_id, kind) where kind <> 'custom'`), `audience_group_members` (`group_id fk audience_groups on delete cascade, person_id fk persons on delete cascade, org_id, added_by, created_at`; PK `(group_id, person_id)`; index `(person_id)`); `assert_same_org` triggers on both FKs (a person from another church raises `23514`/the trigger's errcode — read `app.assert_same_org`); `app.on_org_created()` inserts the six system rows per org (`kind` in `everyone, members, attendees, youth, men, women`). Derivation (DESIGN §4.3): `custom` = **base ∧ row in `audience_group_members`**, where base = `congregation_status in ('member','attendee') and deceased_on is null` — so adding an inactive or deceased person to a group has no effect, and `srv_audience_user_ids(group, org)` only returns persons whose `user_id` has an **active** `org_memberships` row, so a member without an account is reached by content but never by push. `app.user_in_group(null)` is true.
- RLS (1.4, DESIGN §6): `audience_groups` — select: any active member; insert/update/delete: `announcements.create` or `org.settings`. `audience_group_members` — select/insert/delete: the same permission pair **only** (a plain member gets 0 rows); there is no update policy. Every write policy also requires `app.org_writable(org)` (suspended orgs are read-only). Nothing in the schema stops a manager from renaming or deleting a **system** row — the UI and Server Actions must refuse it (Build 4).
- FK actions on the referencing tables, as 1.2 created them: `announcements.audience_group_id` and `documents.audience_group_id` `on delete set null`; `calendars.view_audience_group_id` / `submit_audience_group_id` `on delete set null`; `surveys.audience_group_id` `on delete no action` (DESIGN §4.2) — deleting a group a survey targets raises `23503`. Confirm each in `9999_init.sql` section (3) and for `notifications.audience_group_id` (not stated in the docs) — the delete dialog's copy depends on it.
- `@church/domain` (1.6a/1.6b): `SYSTEM_AUDIENCE_GROUPS` (six kinds in order with the display names copied from the SQL), `audienceKindsFor(p, ctx)`, `AudienceKind`, `PERMISSION_KEYS`, `toDomainError`, `DomainError`; there is **no** Zod schema for groups yet (Build 1 adds one).
- `@church/db` (1.7a) `src/queries/audience-groups.ts`: `listAudienceGroups(db, orgId)` (system rows first in `SYSTEM_AUDIENCE_GROUPS` order, then custom by name), `listGroupMembers(db, groupId)` (`audience_group_members` joined to `directory_persons` in two queries — views have no FKs), `insertCustomGroup`, `renameGroup`, `deleteGroup`, `addGroupMember`, `removeGroupMember`; `src/queries/directory.ts`: `listPersons(orgId, { query })` from `directory_persons` (5.1a/5.2a — filters `org_id = orgId`; the view also returns fellowship-visible persons of other churches), `getPerson(id)`, `listPersonsForHousehold(householdId)`; `src/queries/settings.ts` `getSettings(orgId)`; `queryKeys` in `src/keys.ts` — the family `queryKeys.groups.list(orgId)` and `queryKeys.groups.members(groupId)` already exists (1.7a; 4.2a: "use these exact keys; do not add parallel ones"): extend THAT family additively and never add an `audienceGroups` root, or web and mobile would cache the same rows under two keys and invalidations would miss. Read the real signatures — some take `db` first, some are bound.
- Web (2.1a/3.1/3.2b/3.5a/5.1a/5.4a): `requireOrgMember(slug)` → `OrgContext` (org id spelled `org.orgId` or `org.org_id` — read `src/lib/auth/require-org.ts`), `requirePerm(ctx, perm | perms[])` (an array means any-of), `requireWritable(ctx)`, `isWritable(ctx)`, `hasAnyPerm(ctx, perms)`, `getAuthContext().userId`; `NAV_ITEMS` in `src/features/org/nav.ts` (`{ href, label, requires }`); `ActionResult` / `toActionError` in `src/lib/actions/result.ts`; 3.2b's `src/features/users/PersonPicker.tsx` (a `command`-based searchable list fed by `listLinkablePersons(orgId, search)`, shows "first last · household") — the model for Build 6's picker, not reusable as-is because it hides persons already linked to a user; the audience select at `src/features/audience/AudienceGroupSelect.tsx` (5.4a moved it there and left a re-export at `src/features/announcements/AudienceGroupSelect.tsx`; if 5.4a has not run yet, the component is still at the old path — edit whichever exists and do not move it yourself); 3.7a's Playwright layout: `apps/web/playwright.config.ts` (`testDir: './e2e'`; the `smoke` project collects ONLY files matching `testMatch: /smoke\.spec\.ts/`; 3.7b's `full` project matches `/full\/.*\.spec\.ts/`), the single `apps/web/e2e/smoke.spec.ts`, helpers `apps/web/e2e/helpers/{headers,routes}.ts` (`expectStrictHeaders`), mock env `apps/web/e2e/mock-env.ts`, `pnpm --filter web test:e2e:smoke` — there is no `e2e/smoke/` directory, and a file named `e2e/groups.spec.ts` would not be collected (see Build 10); 3.8's `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` and 1.5's `docs/RLS.md`.

## Build

2. **`@church/db` (additive, same file `src/queries/audience-groups.ts`, each with a test in the module's existing test style)**: `updateCustomGroup(db, { id, name, description })` (do not change `renameGroup`); `addGroupMembers(db, { groupId, orgId, personIds, addedBy })` — one multi-row insert; `listGroupMemberCounts(db, orgId)` — one `select group_id from audience_group_members where org_id = …` reduced to `Record<groupId, number>` (do not issue one count query per group); `countGroupUsage(db, groupId)` → `{ announcements, documents, calendars, surveys }` using `head: true, count: 'exact'` selects on `announcements.audience_group_id`, `documents.audience_group_id`, `calendars` (`view_audience_group_id` or `submit_audience_group_id`), `surveys.audience_group_id`; `listPersonsForPicker(db, orgId, { query, limit: 50 })` — `directory_persons` filtered `org_id = orgId`, `deceased_on is null`, `congregation_status in ('member','attendee')`, ordered by last then first name, selecting only the columns the picker renders (id, names, household id and name, `congregation_status`, `photo_path`, plus `user_id` if the view exposes it — read the view; never `select` from `persons`). `queryKeys.groups.detail(groupId)`, `.groups.counts(orgId)`, `.groups.usage(groupId)`, `.groups.picker(orgId, query)` added additively beside the existing `queryKeys.groups.list(orgId)` / `.groups.members(groupId)` (keep those two untouched; add no `audienceGroups` root).

Create one to target an announcement, document or calendar at a hand-picked list of people." When `!isWritable(ctx)` (suspended) hide every write control and show the 3.1 banner. Add `{ href: 'groups', label: 'Groups', requires: ['announcements.create', 'org.settings'] }` to `NAV_ITEMS` after Documents/Calendars (match how 3.5a/5.3a/5.4a express any-of `requires`; if `requires` only takes one key, extend the type additively with a test).

## Goal
When you finish, the database knows how a person joins a church with a code: a leader holding `users.create` mints an 8-character code (optionally labelled, expiring, limited to N uses, or auto-approving), a signed-in person redeems it with `redeem_join_code` and either becomes an active member at once (auto-approve) or gets a `pending` membership plus a `join_requests` row that a `users.create` holder approves (linking or creating a directory person) or rejects; the requester can cancel. All of it lives in a NEW re-runnable migration `supabase/migrations/9998_join_codes.sql` that the founder pastes after `9999_init.sql`, is covered by a new RLS test file, is exposed through typed wrappers in `@church/db`, validated by Zod schemas and error keys in `@church/domain`, and documented in `docs/MIGRATIONS.md`, `docs/RLS.md`, `supabase/README.md` and the HANDOFF ledger. PLAN §4 states neither fact explicitly, so confirm both by reading the bodies; Build 1 (5) says what to do if 1.3 built them differently. `public.accept_invitation(text)` is the template for "attach a user to an org" (upserts the membership `active`, creates a one-person household + person `created_via = 'invitation'`, `attendee`, merges for an existing member) — read its body; if 1.3 factored the household/person creation into an `app.*` helper, call it instead of copying.

Whether or not `9999_init.sql` has been pasted, **do not edit `9999_init.sql`** in this step — everything goes into the new file.

## Build
1. **`supabase/migrations/9998_join_codes.sql`** — re-runnable, same section skeleton as 9999 (label empty sections with a one-line comment so the structure is recognisable). Header comment: purpose, "paste after `9999_init.sql`; re-paste after any later re-paste of 9999 because 9999's section (4) drops every `ca_%` policy", and the list of objects (re)defined.
   - (0) the same owner `rolbypassrls` assertion as 9999.
   - (2) no enum change (`join_request_status` already has `pending, approved, rejected`). Do not add enum values in this file.
   - (3) `alter table public.join_requests add column if not exists review_note text;` (the reviewer's optional note on approve/reject; ≤ 500 chars enforced in the RPC, not by a constraint) and `create index if not exists join_requests_org_pending_idx on public.join_requests (org_id) where status = 'pending';` (the badge count in 5.6b). Nothing else changes on existing tables.
   - (5) functions, every one `security definer set search_path = ''`, schema-qualified everywhere (`extensions.gen_random_bytes`, `public.join_codes`, `auth.uid()`). **plpgsql name-shadowing rule:** the parameter names below must stay exactly as written (1.7a's `rpc.ts` passes object keys equal to the SQL parameter names), and several shadow column names (`code`, `person_id`, `label`, `auto_approve`, `expires_at`, `max_uses`, `note`); with plpgsql's default `variable_conflict = error` an unqualified `where code = …` fails at runtime with "column reference is ambiguous". So alias every table (`from public.join_codes jc`, `public.join_requests r`, `public.org_memberships m`), qualify every column (`jc.code`, `r.person_id`), and refer to a shadowed parameter by function name (`redeem_join_code.code`, `approve_join_request.person_id`). Never rely on `#variable_conflict use_column`. **Pending-membership prerequisite:** if `public.my_context()` omits `pending` memberships, or `app.member_org_ids()` (or any helper the read policies use) counts `pending` ones, redefine that function in THIS file with `create or replace` and the identical signature (no `drop`) so pending memberships are visible in `my_context()` but grant no reads; state it in the header comment and in HANDOFF 'Deviations from plan'. Test (3) below is the guard for this.
     - `app.generate_join_code() returns text` — 8 characters from the alphabet `ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789` (32 symbols; no `0/O/1/I`, so codes survive being read aloud and printed), each symbol chosen from one byte of `extensions.gen_random_bytes(8)` (`substr(alphabet, (get_byte(b, i) % 32) + 1, 1)`), looping while a row with that `code` exists (give up after 20 attempts with `raise exception … errcode 'P0001', message = 'join_code_generation_failed'`). Store the constant alphabet in one place (a comment says `packages/domain/src/join-codes.ts` mirrors it).
     - `app.attach_joined_user(org uuid, uid uuid, person uuid, approver uuid) returns uuid` (membership id) — the shared body of auto-approve and approve: `insert into public.org_memberships (org_id, user_id, status, approved_by, approved_at) values (org, uid, 'active', approver, now()) on conflict (org_id, user_id) do update set status = 'active', approved_by = excluded.approved_by, approved_at = excluded.approved_at where public.org_memberships.status = 'pending'` (never resurrect a `disabled` membership — callers refuse it earlier); no permissions are granted; when `person` is not null: its `org_id = org` (`cross_org_reference`) and `user_id is null` or already `uid` (else `person_already_linked`, errcode `23505`), then set `persons.user_id = uid`; when `person` is null and no `persons` row in `org` has `user_id = uid`: create a one-person household + person exactly the way `accept_invitation` does, with `households.created_via = 'self'` (DESIGN §4.2 lists `admin | invitation | self`; a joiner creates their own record), `congregation_status = 'attendee'`, names from `profiles.display_name` (split on the first space; fall back to the email local part), `email` from `profiles.email`. If a `check` on `created_via` forbids `'self'`, stop and tell me — do not alter the constraint here.
     - `public.create_join_code(org uuid, label text default null, auto_approve boolean default false, expires_at timestamptz default null, max_uses int default null) returns public.join_codes` — `perform app.require_user(); perform app.require_writable(org);` `app.has_perm(org, 'users.create')` or super admin else `permission_denied` (42501); `max_uses` null or ≥ 1 and `expires_at` null or `> now()` else errcode `22023`, message `invalid_argument`; `label` trimmed, ≤ 80 chars, empty → null; insert with `code = app.generate_join_code()`, `created_by = auth.uid()`; return the row (the code is readable by `users.create` holders anyway).
     - `public.revoke_join_code(code_id uuid) returns void` — load the code (else errcode `P0001`, message `join_code_invalid`); `users.create` in its org; `require_writable`; `update … set revoked_at = coalesce(revoked_at, now())` (idempotent).
     - `public.redeem_join_code(code text, message text default null) returns jsonb` — `uid := app.require_user()`; `normalized := upper(regexp_replace(coalesce(code, ''), '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'))`; find `join_codes` by `code = normalized::extensions.citext`; not found, `revoked_at is not null`, or org `status = 'cancelled'` → errcode `P0001`, message `join_code_invalid`; `expires_at <= now()` → `22023` `join_code_expired`; `max_uses is not null and use_count >= max_uses` → `22023` `join_code_exhausted`; `perform app.require_writable(org)`; then the caller's membership in that org: `active` → return `jsonb_build_object('status', 'already_member', 'org_id', …, 'slug', …, 'name', …)` (no error — the app switches to the church); `disabled` → errcode `42501`, message `membership_disabled`; `pending` → return the existing request as `{status: 'pending', org_id, slug, name, request_id}` without touching `use_count` (idempotent retry). Otherwise `update join_codes set use_count = use_count + 1`; when `auto_approve`: `app.attach_joined_user(org, uid, null, null)`, insert `join_requests` as `approved` with `reviewed_at = now()` (the audit trail of who came in through which code), return `{status: 'active', org_id, slug, name}`; else insert `org_memberships (org_id, user_id, status) values (org, uid, 'pending')` and `join_requests` as `pending` with `message` (trimmed, ≤ 500 chars, empty → null), return `{status: 'pending', org_id, slug, name, request_id}`.
     - `public.approve_join_request(request_id uuid, person_id uuid default null, note text default null) returns uuid` — load the request (else `P0001`, message `join_request_not_found`); `users.create` in `request.org_id` (or super admin) else `permission_denied`; `require_writable`; `status <> 'pending'` → `22023` `join_request_not_pending`; **already a member:** if the requester's membership in that org is already `active` (they accepted an invitation while the request waited — DESIGN §5 path 1), do not raise: skip `attach_joined_user` unless `person_id` is given (then only link that person), mark the request `approved` with `person_id = coalesce(approve_join_request.person_id, <the person already linked to request.user_id in org>)`, and return the existing membership id; otherwise `membership := app.attach_joined_user(org, request.user_id, approve_join_request.person_id, auth.uid())`; update the request `status = 'approved', person_id = coalesce(person_id, (select id from public.persons where org_id = org and user_id = request.user_id)), reviewed_by = auth.uid(), reviewed_at = now(), review_note = nullif(trim(note), '')`; return the membership id.
     - `public.reject_join_request(request_id uuid, note text default null) returns void` — same guards; set `status = 'rejected', reviewed_by, reviewed_at, review_note`; `delete from public.org_memberships where org_id = org and user_id = request.user_id and status = 'pending'` so the person may redeem again later (the partial unique index frees because the request is no longer `pending`).
     - `public.cancel_join_request(request_id uuid) returns void` — `uid := app.require_user()`; the request must exist with `user_id = uid` (else `P0001` `join_request_not_found` — never reveal other people's requests) and be `pending` (else `join_request_not_pending`); delete the request row and the `pending` membership row. No `require_writable`: a person may withdraw from a suspended church too — this is a deliberate deviation from DESIGN §5 ("`app.require_writable` is called at the top of every mutating RPC"); justify it in a comment and record it under HANDOFF 'Deviations from plan'.
     - Add the new keys to the comment-block catalogue at the top of section (5) of THIS file (not 9999): `join_code_invalid P0001`, `join_code_expired 22023`, `join_code_exhausted 22023`, `membership_disabled 42501`, `join_request_not_found P0001`, `join_request_not_pending 22023`, `person_already_linked 23505`, `invalid_argument 22023`, `join_code_generation_failed P0001` (nine keys).
   - (6) no views. (7) no new triggers (`join_requests_touch_updated_at` and the `assert_same_org` triggers exist in 9999; `audit_row` — check whether 9999 attached it to `join_codes`/`join_requests`; if not, add `drop trigger if exists … ; create trigger join_codes_audit …` here using `app.audit_row()` so code creation/revocation and approvals are audited).
   - (8) policies: read 9999's `profiles` select policy. 5.6b must show the requester's name and email to `users.create` holders; if that policy covers only users with an **active** membership in a shared org, add `drop policy if exists ca_profiles_select_join_requesters on public.profiles; create policy ca_profiles_select_join_requesters on public.profiles for select to authenticated using (exists (select 1 from public.join_requests r where r.user_id = profiles.user_id and r.org_id = any ((select app.perm_org_ids('users.create')))))`; if it already covers pending memberships, add nothing and say so in the header comment.
   - (9) grants: `revoke all on function <each of the six public RPCs> from public, anon; grant execute on function <each> to authenticated;` with full signatures; `app.generate_join_code()` and `app.attach_joined_user(…)` get an explicit `revoke all … from public, anon, authenticated` and no grant.
   - (10)/(11): none — one comment line each.
2. **Harness**: `scripts/db/local-up.sh && scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh` — both applies must succeed with the new file. 1.4a's `08_rerunnable.sql` snapshots object/policy/function counts, re-applies ONLY `9999_init.sql` with `\i supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql`, and asserts identical counts — and 9999's section (4) drops every `ca_%` policy, so once this file defines functions and (possibly) `ca_profiles_select_join_requesters`, the re-apply removes them and 08 fails for certain. Fix: add a second line `\i supabase/migrations/9998_join_codes.sql` directly after the 9999 line (with a comment that every later migration is appended here in descending order — 6.1a and 6.3a follow the same rule), keep the psql-only comment 1.4a wrote, and make `check-rerunnable.sh` iterate over every `supabase/migrations/*.sql` if it currently names 9999 alone. Record both changes in HANDOFF.
3. **RLS tests** `supabase/tests/rls/11_join_codes.sql` (leave `10_*` free — G14's 6.1a takes `10_surveys_head_of_house.sql`; a gap in the glob is harmless). Same harness (`begin … rollback`, helpers), inline fixtures: orgs A and B; users `a_admin` (`users.create`), `a_member` (no permissions), `a_disabled` (`disabled` membership), `newcomer` (auth + `profiles` row, no membership), `b_member` (org B). Assertions: (1) `a_admin` creates a code → `char_length = 8`, every character in the alphabet, `use_count = 0`; `a_member` → `assert_denied`; suspended org → `organization_suspended`. (2) `newcomer` redeems the generated code typed lowercase with a dash → `status = 'pending'`; `org_memberships` row `pending`; `join_requests` row `pending` with the message; `use_count = 1`; `my_context()` as `newcomer` lists org A with `membership_status = 'pending'`; redeeming again returns the same `request_id`, `use_count` stays 1. (3) Pending grants nothing: as `newcomer`, `announcements`/`sermons`/`bulletins`/`documents` of org A → 0 rows, `join_requests` → exactly the own row, `join_codes` → 0 rows; `b_member` → 0 `join_requests` rows of org A. (4) `a_member` cannot approve (42501); `a_admin` approves with `person_id = null` → membership `active` with `approved_by = a_admin`, one new household (`created_via = 'self'`) with one `attendee` person whose `user_id = newcomer`, request `approved` with `person_id` set; approving again → `join_request_not_pending`; `srv_audience_user_ids(<everyone group of A>, A)` now contains `newcomer` (call it after `app_test.login_service()` — `srv_*` functions are executable by `service_role` only per `09_grants.sql` — then `app_test.logout()`; if `helpers.sql` has no `login_service`, set `role service_role` the way `08`/`09` do). ## Goal
When you finish, an `https://<DOMAIN>/invite/<token>` link tapped on an Android phone with Anacast installed opens the app directly (Android App Links) instead of the browser: `apps/mobile/app.config.ts` declares a verified `intentFilters` entry for the web host, and the web app serves the Digital Asset Links statement at `https://<DOMAIN>/.well-known/assetlinks.json` from an env-driven Route Handler that lists the founder's signing-certificate fingerprints for package `com.anacast.app`. Separately, a leader editing a YouTube sermon on `/o/<slug>/sermons/<id>` (and the Link tab of `/sermons/new`) has a **Re-check link** button that asks YouTube's oEmbed endpoint, server-side, whether the video is still available and embeddable, and shows the answer (title, channel, or "private / removed / embedding disabled"). `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md`, `docs/MEDIA.md`, `docs/ENV.md` and HANDOFF.md tell the founder how to collect the fingerprints, set the variable, rebuild the APK and verify on a device. No schema change; no new native dependency.

## Inputs / prior state

## Build
1. **Shared constants** in `packages/domain/src/urls.ts` (append, do not rename existing exports): `ANDROID_PACKAGE_ID = 'com.anacast.app'` and `APP_LINK_PATH_PREFIXES = ['/invite'] as const` (the https paths the app claims; `/join` is added by the proposed step 5.9, `/s/*` and `/embed/*` must never be claimed — share pages are meant for the browser). 2. **Mobile intent filter** — edit `apps/mobile/app.config.ts`: compute `webHost` from `process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL` (`new URL(value).host`; when the variable is missing or not an https URL, log one warning with `console.warn` and set no intent filter so `expo export` in CI with the 4.1a mock env still works). When present, set

If `app.config.ts` cannot import `@church/domain` at config-evaluation time (Metro is not involved here — Expo evaluates the config with Node/ts-node; check how 4.1a imports things and whether the domain package's `exports` resolve), copy the two constants into the config file with a comment naming `packages/domain/src/urls.ts` as the source and add a Vitest in `apps/mobile` that imports both and asserts equality (`app-config-parity.test.ts`). Keep the `scheme: 'anacast'` entry; App Links are additional, not a replacement.
3. **Mobile handling check** — do not rewrite 4.1b's parser and add no `app-links.ts`: extend `parseAppLink` in `apps/mobile/src/lib/links.ts` so the https form is accepted ONLY when the URL's host equals `new URL(EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL).host` (pass the host in as a second argument or read `publicEnv().webUrl`; keep the `anacast://` scheme form unchanged). This tightens 4.1b's any-host behaviour — an App Link is only ever delivered for the verified host, and a foreign host must not mint an invite route — so record the change in HANDOFF "Deviations from plan". Tests in the existing `src/lib/links.test.ts`: `https://<web host>/invite/tok123` → invite route with `tok123`; `https://other.example/invite/tok` → `{ kind: 'unknown' }`; `anacast://invite/tok` → unchanged behaviour; a cold start with `Linking.getInitialURL()` returning the https form reaches the same route as a warm `Linking.addEventListener('url')` event (mock `expo-linking`). The invite screen `app/(auth)/invite/[token].tsx` must not care which form delivered the token.
4. **assetlinks route** — create `apps/web/app/.well-known/assetlinks.json/route.ts` (`export const runtime = 'nodejs'`, `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`) with `GET` returning `application/json` and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`. Body: `[{ "relation": ["delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls"], "target": { "namespace": "android_app", "package_name": ANDROID_PACKAGE_ID, "sha256_cert_fingerprints": [...] } }]`. Fingerprints come from the new **server** env var `ANDROID_CERT_SHA256_FINGERPRINTS` (comma-separated, uppercase hex pairs separated by colons — validate each with `/^([0-9A-F]{2}:){31}[0-9A-F]{2}$/`; trim, uppercase, drop empties; reject invalid entries with a 500 and a server log line naming the position, never the value). When the variable is unset or empty return `200 []` (an empty statement list makes Android fall back to the browser, which is the correct pre-launch behaviour and keeps the route valid JSON). Put the parsing in `apps/web/src/lib/app-links/assetlinks.ts` (`buildAssetLinks(fingerprintsEnv)`, `parseFingerprints`) with Vitest: unset → `[]`; one and two fingerprints; lowercase input normalised; malformed → throws. If Next refuses the dot-directory under `app/`, fall back to `app/api/assetlinks/route.ts` plus a `rewrites()` entry in `next.config.ts` mapping `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` to it, and record the deviation.
5. **Proxy and headers** — add `/.well-known/:path*` to the `proxy.ts` matcher exclusions (no session refresh, no redirect on this path). Confirm `next.config.ts` still sends the strict headers on it (harmless for JSON); do not loosen CSP or `X-Frame-Options`. `robots`: leave the `X-Robots-Tag` behaviour as the other public routes have it.
6. **Env plumbing** — `src/lib/env.ts`: add `ANDROID_CERT_SHA256_FINGERPRINTS` to `serverEnv()` as optional (follow the pattern used for `RESEND_API_KEY`). `apps/web/.env.example`: add the variable with an explanatory comment and no value. `docs/ENV.md`: new row — owner founder, location Vercel (server), set in step 5.7a / updated in 6.5 (Play App Signing adds a second fingerprint), behaviour when absent "assetlinks returns `[]`; invite links open in the browser".
7. **YouTube oEmbed client** — `apps/web/src/lib/media/youtube-oembed.ts`: `recheckYouTube(videoId, deps = { fetch: globalThis.fetch, timeoutMs: 5000 })` → GET `https://www.youtube.com/oembed?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3D<id>&format=json` with an `AbortController` timeout and `cache: 'no-store'`. Map: 200 with JSON → `{ status: 'ok', title, authorName, thumbnailUrl }` (only these three fields; ignore the rest); 401 or 403 → `{ status: 'not_embeddable' }` (YouTube answers 401 for embedding-disabled and private videos, 403 for some private/region cases — do not try to tell them apart); 404 → `{ status: 'not_found' }`; anything else, a non-JSON body, a network error or the timeout → `{ status: 'error', detail: 'timeout' | 'network' | `http_${code}` }`. Validate `videoId` with the same 11-character rule `parseMediaLink` uses; throw on anything else. Pure and fully unit-tested with a stubbed `fetch` (200, 401, 403, 404, 500, malformed JSON, abort). Never log the URL or the response body. Copy for each status lives in `src/features/sermons/recheck-copy.ts` (`RECHECK_MESSAGES`): ok → "Available: <title> — <channel>"; not_embeddable → "YouTube reports this video is private or has embedding disabled. Members will not be able to play it in the app."; not_found → "YouTube reports this video was removed or the id is wrong."; error → "Could not reach YouTube right now; try again later." States: idle → "Re-check link"; pending spinner; result line with the `RECHECK_MESSAGES` text and the thumbnail (48 px, `referrerPolicy="no-referrer"`, only when `status = 'ok'`; the CSP `img-src` must already allow `https:` images or the `i.ytimg.com` host — check `buildCsp` in `src/lib/security/csp.ts` and add `https://i.ytimg.com` to `img-src` there (with a `csp.test.ts` case) if needed, recording it); `not_applicable` text for other providers. Remove 3.3a's "Re-check link is step 5.7" wording. When `status = 'ok'` and the sermon title differs from the oEmbed title, show a small "Use this title" link that fills the title field (edit form only; it is just a form value change, the leader still saves).
10. **Playwright** — add a `test.describe('app links')` block to `apps/web/e2e/smoke.spec.ts` (3.7a's `smoke` project matches only `/smoke\.spec\.ts/`, so a new `e2e/app-links.spec.ts` would never run; if you prefer a separate file name it `apps/web/e2e/app-links.smoke.spec.ts` and confirm with `pnpm --filter web exec playwright test --list --project=smoke | grep -c app-links` → ≥ 1), importing `expectStrictHeaders` from `apps/web/e2e/helpers/headers.ts`: `GET /.well-known/assetlinks.json` → 200, `content-type` JSON, body is an array; with the mock env's `ANDROID_CERT_SHA256_FINGERPRINTS` (add one syntactically valid dummy fingerprint of 32 `AA` pairs to `apps/web/e2e/mock-env.ts` AND to the CI web-build step's env in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, keeping the two identical so CI does not rebuild — 3.7a keeps the mock env in that one file, never in `playwright.config.ts`) the array has one statement whose `package_name` is `com.anacast.app`; without it (a second request in a test that stubs the env is not possible at runtime — cover the empty case in Vitest instead); `expectStrictHeaders` on the response; the route is not redirected to `/login`. ## Constraints
- Web and mobile never hold elevated Supabase keys; the Server Action uses the user client under RLS; the oEmbed call is a plain outbound fetch with no credentials. `ANDROID_CERT_SHA256_FINGERPRINTS` is a server variable (fingerprints are public information, but keep the single pattern: config lives in `serverEnv()`), never `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`/`EXPO_PUBLIC_*`.

In the browser: sign in as a leader with `sermons.link`, open a YouTube sermon, click Re-check link with a public video id → "Available: …"; with a known-private id → the not_embeddable text; with the network disabled (DevTools offline does not affect the server — instead stub `timeoutMs: 1` via a temporary env in dev if you want to see the error text). - Device verification is impossible in this session (no device, and App Links need a signed build whose fingerprint matches); say so in the final message and point the founder at the `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` section.

## Goal
When you finish, a directory administrator (a member holding `users.create` or `org.settings`) can bring an existing congregation list into Anacast at `/o/<slug>/directory/import`: download a CSV template, upload or paste a CSV of up to 2,000 rows (one row per person, grouped into households by a `household_key` column), see a **dry run** that lists exactly what would be created (households, persons, roles, congregation status) and every error by row and column (bad dates, unknown values, two heads in one household, missing names, conflicting household fields, rows over the cap) plus "possible duplicate" warnings against people already in the directory, and only when there are zero errors click **Import**, which creates the rows in batches through the existing RPCs `save_household`, `save_person` and `set_congregation_status` under RLS with a progress bar and a final report. Imported households follow the founder's privacy rule for admin-created households (hidden from the fellowship until a family adult confirms in the app) and the import page says so. The CSV is never stored anywhere; the parser and validator are pure functions in `@church/domain` with a shared sample fixture; `docs/DIRECTORY_IMPORT.md` documents the columns and rules. No schema change.

## Inputs / prior state
- Schema (1.2–1.4, frozen or not — read `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` sections (3), (5), (8)): `households` (`name` not null, `address_line1/2`, `city`, `region`, `postal_code`, `country` default `'US'`, `home_phone`, `anniversary date`, `sort_key`, `hide_from_fellowship`, `hide_from_congregation`, `show_children_in_fellowship`, `privacy_confirmed_by/at`, `created_via text default 'admin'`), `persons` (`household_id` not null, `first_name`/`last_name` not null, `preferred_name`, `sex`, `birthdate`, `birthdate_visibility` default `month_day`, `marital_status` default `unknown`, `household_role` default `other`, `congregation_status` default `attendee`, `member_since`, `youth_override`, `directory_listed` default true, `email citext`, `mobile_phone`, `work_phone`, `deceased_on`), the partial unique index for one `head` per household (orchestrator decision 6), `guard_household_privacy_columns`, and the admin-created default `hide_from_fellowship = true` (DESIGN §13 risk 15). RPCs: `save_household(jsonb)` → uuid, `save_person(jsonb)` → uuid, `set_congregation_status(person_id, status, member_since)`; error keys in `@church/domain` `errors.ts` (1.6b) — read the catalogue for `duplicate`, `field_not_editable`, `head_already_set` or whatever 1.3 named the one-head violation, `organization_suspended`.
- `@church/domain` (1.6a/1.6b): `schemas/directory.ts` with `saveHouseholdSchema`, `savePersonSchema` (payload whitelists), enum literal lists (`SEX`, `MARITAL_STATUS`, `HOUSEHOLD_ROLE`, `CONGREGATION_STATUS`, `BIRTHDATE_VISIBILITY` — use the exported names you find), `audiences.ts` (`personAge`, `isMinor`), `dates.ts` (org timezone helpers), `fixtures/persons.json`.
- `@church/db` (1.7a, 5.1a/5.1b): `queries/directory.ts` — `searchHouseholds(orgId, { query, limit, offset })`, `listPersonsForHousehold(householdId)`, `listPersonsForHouseholds(householdIds)`, `getPerson(id)` (web code never issues ad-hoc `.from(...)` queries — 5.1a's rule; Build 4 adds one query helper here); RPC wrappers `saveHousehold(db, { payload })`, `savePerson(db, { payload })`, `setCongregationStatus(db, { person_id, status, member_since })`; `getSettings(orgId)` (settings module) for `adult_min_age`, `youth_*`, `timezone`.
- Web (3.1, 5.1a, 5.1b): `requireOrgMember(orgSlug)` → ctx (`orgId` or `org_id` — read `src/lib/auth/require-org.ts`), `requireDirectoryAdmin(ctx)` and `isDirectoryAdmin(ctx)` in `src/lib/auth/require-directory-admin.ts`, `requireWritable(ctx)`, `NAV_ITEMS` in `src/features/org/nav.ts`, the households list `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/directory/page.tsx` + `src/features/directory/HouseholdsPage.tsx` whose empty state says "No households yet — create the first one or import a CSV (step 5.7)", `HouseholdForm`, `PersonForm`, `derive-badges.ts`, the `ActionResult` shape and `sonner` toasts, `apps/web/e2e/directory.spec.ts` (5.1a's smoke checks — but note 3.7a's `smoke` project collects only files matching `testMatch: /smoke\.spec\.ts/` in `apps/web/playwright.config.ts`, so unless a later step widened it that file is NOT collected; Build 6 handles this) with helpers in `apps/web/e2e/helpers/headers.ts` (`expectStrictHeaders`), and `e2e/full/01-acceptance.spec.ts` + `e2e/full/supabase-admin.ts` (3.7b, env-gated `full` project), `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` (3.8).
- Founder decisions that apply: "admin-entered households start hidden from the fellowship until a family adult confirms; leaders can only make a family *more* private" (HANDOFF Decisions) — imports are admin-entered; decision 3 (each church sets its own youth/adult ages → age rules read `organization_settings`); orchestrator decision 6 (at most one `head` per household; head of house is what surveys use in 6.1); decision 7 (a `suspended` church rejects writes → the import page shows the 3.1 banner and disables Import); PLAN §4 permission mapping (directory admin = `users.create` or `org.settings`).

## Build
1. **Column spec and parser** — `packages/domain/src/directory-import.ts` (pure, no Node APIs):
   - `DIRECTORY_IMPORT_COLUMNS`: ordered list of `{ key, required, kind, help }` — `household_key`* (free text; rows with the same key form one household), `household_name`* (taken from the first row of the group; other rows must be empty or identical), `address_line1`, `address_line2`, `city`, `region`, `postal_code`, `country` (default `US`), `home_phone`, `anniversary`, `first_name`*, `last_name`*, `preferred_name`, `sex` (`male`/`female`), `birthdate`, `birthdate_visibility` (`full`/`month_day`/`hidden`; default `month_day`), `marital_status` (the enum's values; default `unknown`), `household_role` (`head`/`spouse`/`child`/`other`; default `other`), `congregation_status` (`member`/`attendee`/`inactive`; default `attendee`), `member_since`, `email`, `mobile_phone`, `work_phone`, `directory_listed` (`yes`/`no`/`true`/`false`; default yes). Column order in the file is free; matching is by header name, case- and whitespace-insensitive; unknown headers are a warning, not an error; a missing required header is a file-level error.
   - `parseCsv(text)`: a small RFC 4180 parser (quoted fields, doubled quotes, embedded commas and newlines, CRLF/LF, optional UTF-8 BOM, trailing empty line ignored, ragged rows → row error `ragged_row`). No dependency (a dependency needs founder approval; say so in a comment). Reject input over `DIRECTORY_IMPORT_MAX_BYTES = 1_000_000` or more than `DIRECTORY_IMPORT_MAX_ROWS = 2000` data rows with a file-level error before parsing further.
   - `validateDirectoryImport(rows, ctx: { settings: { adult_min_age, timezone }, today })` → `{ households: PlannedHousehold[], errors: ImportIssue[], warnings: ImportIssue[], counts }` where `ImportIssue = { row: number (1-based data row, 0 = file), column?: string, code: ImportIssueCode, message: string }`. Codes (exhaustive union, each with a message in `DIRECTORY_IMPORT_MESSAGES`): `missing_required`, `unknown_value` (enum), `bad_date` (accept `YYYY-MM-DD` and `MM/DD/YYYY` only; normalise to ISO), `future_date`, `household_conflict` (differing household fields within one key), `multiple_heads`, `too_long` (names ≤ 120, address lines ≤ 200, phones ≤ 40, emails ≤ 254 — align with `savePersonSchema`/`saveHouseholdSchema` limits; reuse those Zod schemas per planned row so the RPC never sees a payload the UI could not send), `bad_email`, `ragged_row`, `too_many_rows`, `file_too_large`, `missing_header`, and warnings `unknown_header`, `child_without_birthdate` (role `child` and no birthdate — the age rules will treat the person by role alone, PLAN §4 derivation), `possible_duplicate` (filled in server-side, Build 4). Normalise enums case-insensitively (`Male` → `male`), trim every cell, treat empty as null, `preferred_name` empty → null.

   - Fixture `packages/domain/fixtures/directory-import.sample.csv` (12 rows, 4 households, every optional column used at least once, one intentional error per error code in a sibling `directory-import.errors.csv`). Vitest `directory-import.test.ts`: parser cases (quotes, BOM, CRLF, embedded newline, ragged), header matching, every issue code fires exactly where expected against the errors fixture, the sample fixture produces zero errors and the expected counts, template round-trips through the parser with zero errors, date normalisation, 2,001 rows → `too_many_rows`. Add an "Import CSV" button to the households toolbar in `HouseholdsPage.tsx` (directory admins only) and change 5.1a's empty-state text to a link "import a CSV" → `directory/import`. No `NAV_ITEMS` entry (it is a sub-page of Directory). A suspended church (`!isWritable(ctx)`) shows the 3.1 banner and the Import button stays disabled while dry run still works.
3. **Client flow** — `ImportPage.tsx` (client, three panels):
   - **Prepare**: `TemplateDownloadButton` (builds a Blob from `buildTemplateCsv()`, file name `anacast-directory-template.csv`), a file input (`accept=".csv,text/csv"`, read with `File.text()`; refuse > 1 MB client-side with the `file_too_large` message) and a textarea for pasting; a privacy note: "The file is checked on our server and discarded; nothing is stored until you click Import."
   - **Dry run**: on "Check file" call the Server Action `dryRunDirectoryImportAction(orgSlug, { csv })` (Build 4). Render `ImportSummary` (households to create, persons by role and status, warnings count), `ImportIssuesTable` (errors first, then warnings; columns row / column / message; "Download issues as CSV" via Blob), and `ImportPreview` (accordion per household: name, address line, persons with role/status badges, "possible duplicate" badge with the matched existing name). Checkbox "Skip rows flagged as possible duplicates" (default off).

Clicking shows a confirm dialog with the counts and the sentence "Imported households are hidden from the fellowship directory until a family adult confirms their privacy settings in the app; leaders can only make a family more private (founder decision)." Then the client loops over household batches calling `commitDirectoryImportBatchAction(orgSlug, { csv, householdKeys, skipDuplicates })` with `DIRECTORY_IMPORT_BATCH_SIZE = 20` household keys per call, showing a progress bar (households done / total) and stopping at the first failed batch. Final report: created households/persons, skipped duplicates, and — on failure — the failing row, the domain error message, and the advice "Remove the rows already imported (they now appear in the directory) and check the file again; re-running is safe because imported people are flagged as possible duplicates."
4. **Server Actions** — `src/features/directory/import/actions.ts` (`'use server'`; both: `requireOrgMember(orgSlug)` → `requireDirectoryAdmin(ctx)`; Zod-validate input with `directoryImportRequestSchema` = `{ csv: string.max(1_000_000), householdKeys?: string[].max(20), skipDuplicates?: boolean }`; never trust a client-supplied plan — the server re-parses and re-validates the CSV on every call):

Return the plan (households with persons), issues and counts. Cap the response: when errors exceed 500 return the first 500 plus `truncated: true`.
   - `commitDirectoryImportBatchAction`: `requireWritable(ctx)`; re-run the dry run server-side; refuse with `{ ok: false, error: { key: 'import_has_errors' } }` if any error remains (the client should never get here, but a second admin may have changed settings between calls); then, for each requested `householdKey` in file order: skip if every person is a flagged duplicate and `skipDuplicates`; `saveHousehold(db, { payload: { org_id, ...householdPayload } })` → household id; for each person `savePerson(db, { payload: { org_id, household_id, ...personPayload } })` (skip flagged duplicates when `skipDuplicates`) → person id; when `congregation_status !== 'attendee'` or `member_since` is set call `setCongregationStatus(db, { person_id, status, member_since })` — 5.1b's rule: status and `member_since` never travel through `save_person`, so the audit trail stays uniform. Sequential awaits (no `Promise.all` — RLS-scoped RPCs and the one-head index make ordering matter: import the `head` row first within each household so a `multiple_heads` race is impossible). `export const maxDuration = 60` on the page's segment config for the action. On a thrown domain error return `{ ok: false, error: { key, row, householdKey }, progress: { households, persons } }`; map error keys through `toDomainError` and the domain's `DOMAIN_ERROR_MESSAGES`. Return `{ ok: true, created: { households, persons }, skipped }` otherwise.
   - Idempotency across retries: a household whose persons all match existing people is reported, not re-created, when `skipDuplicates` is on; document that with the checkbox off a retry can create duplicates and that the dry run shows them first.
   - Add error keys `import_has_errors` and `import_batch_failed` to the web-side message map (not to `@church/domain` `errors.ts`, which mirrors DB errcodes only).

## Constraints
- Every write goes through the existing client RPCs with the user-scoped client under RLS — no service client, no direct table inserts, no `srv_*` call, no new RPC or migration (an atomic `srv_import_directory(jsonb)` would be better engineering but needs a migration and a decision; it is recorded as an open issue, not built here). Never `supabase db push` / `db reset`; do not touch `supabase/migrations/`.
- Never store the CSV (no bucket, no table, no log line containing a cell value); do not log names, emails or phones on failure — log only row numbers and issue codes. Server Action payloads are ≤ 1 MB; if Next's default `serverActions.bodySizeLimit` rejects a file near the cap, raise it to `2mb` in `next.config.ts` and record it.
- Reuse `saveHouseholdSchema` / `savePersonSchema` for the per-row payloads so the import can never send a field the person form could not; do not widen those schemas. Do not send `hide_from_fellowship`, `hide_from_congregation`, `show_children_in_fellowship`, `photo_path`, `youth_override` or `deceased_on`.
- Directory reads only through `directory_persons` / `directory_households` (DESIGN §13 risk 14 — `select *` on the base tables fails for clients).
- No new runtime dependency (no papaparse, no csv-parse); the parser lives in `@church/domain`. Pins: Next 16.3, React 19.2.3, Zod 4.5, TypeScript ~5.9, Playwright 1.62. No model identifiers, no secrets, `<slug>@example.test` addresses only in fixtures and tests.
- Do not build updates of existing people, photo import, mobile UI, or the member web directory; do not change 5.1a/5.1b behaviour beyond the toolbar button and the empty-state link.

With `E2E_MODE=full` and the 3.7b env: `pnpm --filter web test:e2e:full` → the directory-import chapter passes (or, without the env, the chapter is skipped with the documented reason).
- Local manual check against the local DB seed (`scripts/db/local-up.sh` and a dev web env pointing at it, as 5.1a documented): download the template, open it in a spreadsheet, add three households, save as CSV, upload → dry run counts match; introduce `head` twice in one household → `multiple_heads` on the right row; `13/45/2020` → `bad_date`; import → households appear with the two privacy badges; open a person → `member_since` and `congregation_status` show what the file said; `audit_log` has rows for every `save_household`/`save_person`/`set_congregation_status` call (`select count(*) from audit_log where …` in psql). Re-upload → duplicates flagged; Skip on → nothing created.
- Suspended check: set the org `status = 'suspended'` in psql → the import page shows the banner and Import is disabled; dry run still works; reset the status.

## 5.10 — Checkpoint D: Phase 2 trial (founder, about 90 minutes; needs an Android phone with USB debugging or the ability to sideload)

Do this after 5.7c is ticked. It repeats the 4.5 pattern (build → sideload → sign in) with the App Links steps 5.7a documented, then runs the two Phase 2 acceptance documents.

1. **Collect the signing-certificate fingerprints.** In the repo root: `npx eas-cli credentials -p android` → choose the project → `preview` build profile → Keystore → copy the line "SHA256 Fingerprint" (32 colon-separated hex pairs). If a `production` profile with its own keystore exists, repeat and keep both. Never paste a fingerprint into a Claude Code prompt or chat — it is not secret, but `prompt_history.txt` is committed; type it into Vercel only.
2. **Set the web variable.** vercel.com → team `Anacast` → the web project → Settings → Environment Variables → Add `ANDROID_CERT_SHA256_FINGERPRINTS` = the fingerprint(s), comma-separated, for the **Production** and **Preview** environments → Save → Deployments → ⋯ on the latest production deployment → Redeploy.
3. **Check the statement.** In a terminal: `curl -s https://<DOMAIN>/.well-known/assetlinks.json` → a JSON array with one statement whose `package_name` is `com.anacast.app` and whose `sha256_cert_fingerprints` lists what you entered (uppercase). An empty `[]` means the variable is missing or the redeploy has not finished.
4. **Build a fresh preview APK** (5.7a changed native config — the old APK cannot verify App Links): `npx eas-cli build -p android --profile preview` → wait for the build → download the APK from the EAS build page → install it on the phone (uninstall the 4.5 APK first if the installer complains about signatures).
5. **Verify App Links on the device.** With the phone connected: `adb shell pm get-app-links com.anacast.app` → the web host shows `verified`. If it shows `none` or `1024`, run `adb shell pm verify-app-links --re-verify com.anacast.app`, wait a minute, repeat. Then send yourself an invite from `/o/<slug>/users` → open the email on the phone (Gmail or another mail app, not the Chrome address bar) → tap the link → Anacast opens on the invite screen.
6. **Web acceptance.** Open `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md`, chapter "Phase 2 trial (Checkpoint D)", and click through it once as the super admin and once as the first church admin (directory → groups → announcement to a group → calendars and event approval → documents → join code sheet → CSV import → YouTube re-check). Tick each item or write the observation down.
7. **Android acceptance.** Open `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md`, section "Phase 2 device checklist (consolidated)", and run every block on the phone (directory and household self-service, calendar, documents, join with a code, App Link). Tick or note.
8. **Record.** In `HANDOFF.md` add under "Environment status" the EAS build id and date, the fingerprint count you entered (not the values), and under a new heading "Checkpoint D observations" every item that did not pass, one line each (what you did, what you saw, what you expected).
